Turkish · 1,000 words

Turkish words 801–900

Turkish words 801 to 900, by how often they're used, each with its meaning in English, an example sentence and, for verbs, the main forms (he, she or it). 49 of them are taught in the lessons of the course.

Learn them with spaced repetition, Anki-style: open the flashcards. Free, no account needed.

Overview1–100101–200201–300301–400401–500501–600601–700701–800801–900901–1000
  1. 801
    ilerlemekverb

    to make progress, to improve; to move forward, to advance

    Türkçen çok ilerlemiş!

    Your Turkish has really improved!

    aorist ilerler · present ilerliyor · past ilerledi · future ilerleyecek

    From ileri (forward). The e becomes i before -(I)yor: ilerliyor. İlerleme = progress.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 10: As long as, unless, in case

  2. 802
    atlamakverb

    to jump; to skip, to leave out

    Çocuk havuza atladı.

    The child jumped into the pool.

    aorist atlar · present atlıyor · past atladı · future atlayacak

    Where you jump takes the dative: suya atlamak. Also to skip: Bu soruyu atla (Skip this question). The a becomes ı before -(I)yor: atlıyor.

    A2

  3. 803
    ayakkabınoun

    shoe

    Yeni ayakkabılarım biraz dar.

    My new shoes are a bit tight.

    Ayak (foot) + kap (container). Ayakkabı numaran kaç? = What's your shoe size? In Turkish homes, shoes usually come off at the door.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 10: Whose is it?

  4. 804
    barnoun

    bar, pub

    Akşam bir barda buluştuk.

    We met at a bar in the evening.

    A loanword, as in English. A café is kafe; a traditional tavern serving rakı and meze is a meyhane.

    B1

  5. 805
    tebriklerinterjection

    congratulations

    Yeni işin için tebrikler!

    Congratulations on your new job!

    Tebrik ederim is a little more formal. Tebrikler can be said to anyone; Aferin (well done) is said to a child or someone younger.

    A2

  6. 806
    olasıadjective

    possible, likely; potential

    Her olası sonucu düşündün mü?

    Have you thought about every possible outcome?

    A little formal; in speech mümkün or muhtemel are more common. Olasılık = probability, possibility.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 2: -DIr: assumption and authority

  7. 807
    etkinoun

    effect, influence; impact

    Bu ilacın etkisi ne zaman başlar?

    When does this medicine start working?

    Etkilemek = to affect, to impress; etkili = effective. The effect of X on Y: X'in Y üzerindeki etkisi.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 3: Complex nominalizations

  8. 808
    kıyafetnoun

    clothes, clothing; outfit

    Düğüne hangi kıyafeti giyeceksin?

    Which outfit are you going to wear to the wedding?

    One kıyafet can be a whole outfit; kıyafetler = clothes. Synonyms: giysi, and elbise (also a dress).

    A2

  9. 809
    şüpheliadjective

    suspicious; doubtful; suspect (noun)

    Kapının önünde şüpheli bir adam var.

    There's a suspicious man in front of the door.

    From şüphe (doubt, suspicion). As a noun, the suspect in a crime: Şüpheli kaçtı (The suspect escaped).

    B1

  10. 810
    kâğıtnoun

    paper; a sheet of paper; playing card

    Bir kâğıt ve kalem verir misin?

    Could you give me a piece of paper and a pen?

    accusative kâğıdı

    Spelled with â (TDK). The t becomes d before a vowel: kâğıdı. Kâğıt oynamak = to play cards.

    A2

  11. 811
    indirmekverb

    to lower, to put down, to take down; to download; to drop off (a passenger); to reduce (a price)

    Beni köşede indirir misiniz?

    Could you drop me off at the corner?

    aorist indirir · present indiriyor · past indirdi · future indirecek

    Causative of inmek (to go down, to get off). Silahını indir! = Put the gun down! İndirim = discount.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 8: Spoken Turkish

  12. 812
    gezegennoun

    planet

    Güneş sisteminde sekiz gezegen var.

    There are eight planets in the solar system.

    From gezmek (to wander), like the Greek word behind planet. Dünya = the Earth; the world.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 3: Complex nominalizations

  13. 813
    bankanoun

    bank

    Banka saat beşte kapanıyor.

    The bank closes at five.

    Banka hesabı = bank account; bankamatik or ATM = cash machine.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 5: Where things are

  14. 814
    vazgeçmekverb

    to give up (on); to change your mind

    Hayallerinden vazgeçme!

    Don't give up on your dreams!

    aorist vazgeçer · present vazgeçiyor · past vazgeçti · future vazgeçecek

    What you give up takes the ablative: bu fikirden vazgeçmek. Alone, to change your mind: Vazgeçtim, gelmiyorum (I changed my mind, I'm not coming).

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 2: Used to, was going to, should have

  15. 815
    sertadjective

    hard, tough; harsh, strict; strong (coffee, wind)

    Bu ekmek çok sert.

    This bread is very hard.

    Opposite of yumuşak (soft). Of people, strict or harsh: sert bir öğretmen; of coffee or wind, strong: sert bir rüzgâr.

    A2

  16. 816
    borçnoun

    debt; what you owe

    Sana ne kadar borcum var?

    How much do I owe you?

    accusative borcu

    The ç becomes c before a vowel: borcu. Borç vermek = to lend; borç almak = to borrow; Borcum ne kadar? = How much do I owe? (in a shop).

    A2

  17. 817
    sayınadjective

    Dear (in formal letters); respected (formal title)

    Sayın yolcularımız, uçağımız İstanbul'a iniyor.

    Dear passengers, our plane is landing in Istanbul.

    Formal, before a surname, a full name or a title, in letters and announcements: Sayın Ayşe Demir, Sayın Yetkili (To whom it may concern). In everyday speech, Bey and Hanım follow the first name instead.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 5: Formal Turkish

  18. 818
    sigaranoun

    cigarette

    Burada sigara içmek yasak.

    Smoking is not allowed here.

    Sigara içmek = to smoke, literally to drink a cigarette. Sigarayı bıraktım = I quit smoking.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 4: Habits and truths: the aorist

  19. 819
    ağıradjective

    heavy; serious (an illness, an injury); slow

    Bu valiz çok ağır, yardım eder misin?

    This suitcase is very heavy; can you help?

    Opposite of hafif (light). Also serious, ağır yaralı (seriously injured), and slow, ağır ağır (slowly).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 8: Comparing

  20. 820
    çoğupronoun

    most (of them); most

    Arkadaşlarımın çoğu İstanbul'da yaşıyor.

    Most of my friends live in Istanbul.

    Çok + the possessive: arkadaşlarımın çoğu (most of my friends), çoğumuz (most of us). Before a noun: çoğu insan (most people). Çoğu zaman = most of the time.

    A2

  21. 821
    hastalıknoun

    illness, disease

    Ciddi bir hastalık değil, merak etme.

    It's not a serious illness; don't worry.

    accusative hastalığı

    Hasta (ill) + -lIk; the k becomes ğ before a vowel: hastalığı. Hastalanmak = to fall ill.

    A2

  22. 822
    tuvaletnoun

    toilet, washroom

    Affedersiniz, tuvalet nerede?

    Excuse me, where's the washroom?

    In a restaurant also lavabo (more discreet) or WC; at home, the bathroom is banyo. Tuvalet kâğıdı = toilet paper.

    A1

  23. 823
    susmakverb

    to be quiet, to stop talking; to keep silent

    Sus, bebek uyuyor!

    Quiet, the baby's sleeping!

    aorist susar · present susuyor · past sustu · future susacak

    Sus! = Be quiet! (blunt); politer: Lütfen sessiz olun. Not to be confused with susamak (to get thirsty).

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 10: As long as, unless, in case

  24. 824
    iğrençadjective

    disgusting, gross; revolting

    Bu koku iğrenç!

    This smell is disgusting!

    Strong and colloquial. From iğrenmek (to be disgusted, by: ablative). Milder: Hiç güzel değil.

    B1

  25. 825
    tatnoun

    taste, flavour

    Bu çorbanın tadı çok güzel.

    This soup tastes really good.

    accusative tadı

    One of the few one-syllable words whose t becomes d before a vowel: tadı. Tadına bakmak = to taste; tatlı = sweet.

    A2

  26. 826
    dolayıpostposition

    because of, due to (after the ablative)

    Kardan dolayı okullar tatil.

    Schools are closed because of the snow.

    Follows the ablative: yağmurdan dolayı. Close to yüzünden (often for something bad) and nedeniyle (formal). Dolayısıyla = consequently.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 9: Where and when: postpositions

  27. 827
    kimliknoun

    identity; ID card (kimlik kartı)

    Kimliğinizi görebilir miyim?

    May I see your ID?

    accusative kimliği

    Kim (who) + -lIk; the k becomes ğ before a vowel: kimliği. Kimlik kartı, or just kimlik = ID card.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 4: Noun clauses

  28. 828
    kenarnoun

    edge, side; shore, bank (of the sea, a river)

    Deniz kenarında bir evleri var.

    They have a house by the sea.

    Used like a place noun: masanın kenarında (on the edge of the table). Deniz kenarı = seaside; yol kenarı = roadside; kenara çekmek = to pull over.

    A2

  29. 829
    zevknoun

    pleasure, enjoyment; taste (in style)

    Seninle çalışmak bir zevk.

    It's a pleasure working with you.

    Zevk almak = to enjoy, with the ablative: müzikten zevk almak. Zevkine göre = to your taste; zevkli = tasteful.

    B1

  30. 830
    birliknoun

    unity, solidarity; union, association; unit (of an army)

    Birlik olursak kazanırız.

    If we stand together, we'll win.

    accusative birliği

    Bir + -lIk; the k becomes ğ before a vowel: birliği. Birlik olmak = to unite; Avrupa Birliği = the European Union. Not birlikte (together).

    B1

  31. 831
    korkunoun

    fear; horror (korku filmi)

    Korku filmlerini hiç sevmem.

    I don't like horror movies at all.

    From korkmak (to be afraid). Korku filmi = horror movie; korkunç = terrible, awful.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 8: Converbs II: the more, whenever, because

  32. 832
    eskidenadverb

    in the past, formerly; used to (with a past verb)

    Eskiden burada bir sinema vardı.

    There used to be a movie theatre here.

    Eski (old) + the ablative. Often with -(I)rdI for past habits: Eskiden çok kitap okurdum (I used to read a lot).

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 2: Was, were, and once upon a time

  33. 833
    sarhoşadjective

    drunk

    Dün gece çok sarhoştun.

    You were very drunk last night.

    Sarhoş olmak = to get drunk. Also figurative: mutluluktan sarhoş (drunk with happiness).

    B1

  34. 834
    teslim etmekverb

    to deliver, to hand over; to hand in; to turn in (someone)

    Ödevimi yarın teslim edeceğim.

    I'll hand in my homework tomorrow.

    aorist teslim eder · present teslim ediyor · past teslim etti · future teslim edecek

    To whom: dative, paketi müşteriye teslim etmek. Teslim olmak = to surrender, to give yourself up: Polise teslim oldu.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 7: Stacked voices

  35. 835
    dolaşmakverb

    to wander, to walk around; to travel around, to tour; to go around

    Bütün gün şehirde dolaştık.

    We wandered around the city all day.

    aorist dolaşır · present dolaşıyor · past dolaştı · future dolaşacak

    Where takes the locative (parkta dolaşmak) or the accusative (dünyayı dolaşmak, to travel around the world). Dolaşmaya çıkmak = to go for a walk.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 1: Unreal conditionals and wishes

  36. 836
    imkânsızadjective

    impossible

    Bu kadar işi bir günde bitirmek imkânsız.

    It's impossible to finish this much work in one day.

    Spelled with â (TDK): imkân (possibility) + -sIz. Synonym: olanaksız; opposite: mümkün.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 4: Noun clauses

  37. 837
    kahramannoun

    hero; main character (of a story)

    Babam benim kahramanım.

    My dad is my hero.

    Also the main character of a novel or a film. Kahramanlık = heroism; halk kahramanı = folk hero.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 7: Discourse and argument

  38. 838
    tehditnoun

    threat

    Bu bir tehdit mi?

    Is that a threat?

    accusative tehdidi

    The t becomes d before a vowel: tehdidi. Tehdit etmek = to threaten: Beni tehdit mi ediyorsun?

    B1

  39. 839
    dövmekverb

    to beat (up), to hit; to pound, to beat (meat, eggs)

    Onu kim dövdü?

    Who beat him up?

    aorist döver · present dövüyor · past dövdü · future dövecek

    To hit someone again and again. Dövüşmek = to fight each other; dövme = tattoo.

    B1

  40. 840
    yanmakverb

    to burn, to be on fire; to be on (a light); to get sunburned

    Mutfakta bir şey yanıyor!

    Something's burning in the kitchen!

    aorist yanar · present yanıyor · past yandı · future yanacak

    Intransitive; to burn something is yakmak. Of a light: Işık yanıyor (The light is on). Güneşte yandım = I got sunburned.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 3: Hearsay and inference

  41. 841
    siyahnoun

    black

    Siyah çantam nerede?

    Where's my black bag?

    Like the other colour words, a noun and an adjective. Siyah is the everyday colour word; kara is mostly figurative or in set phrases (Karadeniz).

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 2: Vowel harmony and plurals

  42. 842
    saçmanoun

    nonsense; absurd, ridiculous (as an adjective); shot (for a shotgun)

    Saçma! Buna kimse inanmaz.

    Nonsense! Nobody will believe that.

    Often an adjective: Bu çok saçma (That's ridiculous). Saçmalamak = to talk nonsense: Saçmalama! Saçma sapan = nonsensical.

    B1

  43. 843
    etnoun

    meat; flesh

    Ben et yemiyorum, vejetaryenim.

    I don't eat meat; I'm vegetarian.

    Kırmızı et = red meat; dana eti = beef; tavuk eti = chicken. Not the imperative et of etmek.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 8: Definite objects

  44. 844
    önemnoun

    importance

    Bunun hiç önemi yok.

    That doesn't matter at all.

    Önemli = important; önem vermek = to care about, to value (dative); Önemi yok = It doesn't matter.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 3: Complex nominalizations

  45. 845
    saklanmakverb

    to hide (yourself); to be kept, to be stored

    Kedi yine yatağın altına saklandı.

    The cat hid under the bed again.

    aorist saklanır · present saklanıyor · past saklandı · future saklanacak

    Reflexive of saklamak (to hide something, to keep). Where takes the dative (dolaba saklanmak) or the locative (dolapta saklanmak). Saklambaç = hide-and-seek.

    B1

  46. 846
    sıkıadjective

    tight, firm; strict; close (friends)

    Ali ile Can çok sıkı arkadaş.

    Ali and Can are very close friends.

    Sıkı çalışmak = to work hard; Sıkı tutun! = Hold on tight! Sıkı fıkı = very close, thick as thieves. Not sık (often).

    B1

  47. 847
    üyenoun

    member

    Ben bu kulübün üyesiyim.

    I'm a member of this club.

    Üye olmak = to become a member, to join (dative: kulübe üye olmak). Üyelik = membership.

    B1

  48. 848
    hizmetnoun

    service

    Bu otelde hizmet çok iyi.

    The service at this hotel is very good.

    Hizmet etmek = to serve (dative). Hizmetinizdeyim = At your service.

    B1

  49. 849
    randevunoun

    appointment; date (romantic)

    Doktordan randevu aldım.

    I made an appointment with the doctor.

    Randevu almak = to make an appointment, from someone: ablative. A date with someone is also randevu, or colloquially buluşma.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 6: Must and need

  50. 850
    zenginadjective

    rich, wealthy

    Çok zengin bir ailenin kızı.

    She's the daughter of a very rich family.

    Opposite of fakir or yoksul (poor). As a noun, a rich person: zenginler. Zenginlik = wealth.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 2: Was, were, and once upon a time

  51. 851
    kedinoun

    cat

    Bahçede küçük bir kedi var.

    There's a little cat in the garden.

    Istanbul is known for its street cats, fed by whole neighbourhoods. A kitten is yavru kedi.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 9: My family

  52. 852
    seçeneknoun

    option, choice; alternative

    Başka bir seçeneğimiz yok.

    We have no other choice.

    accusative seçeneği

    From seçmek (to choose); the k becomes ğ before a vowel: seçeneği. Synonym: alternatif.

    B1

  53. 853
    dükkânnoun

    shop, store

    Köşedeki dükkân pazar günü açık.

    The shop on the corner is open on Sunday.

    Spelled with â (TDK). Usually a small shop; a big store is a mağaza. Dükkâncı = shopkeeper.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 2: Used to, was going to, should have

  54. 854
    karşılıknoun

    response, reply; equivalent; in return (karşılığında)

    Bu kelimenin İngilizce karşılığı ne?

    What's the English equivalent of this word?

    accusative karşılığı

    The k becomes ğ before a vowel: karşılığı. Karşılık vermek = to answer back; karşılığında = in return for: Yardımı karşılığında para istemedi.

    B1

  55. 855
    risknoun

    risk

    Bu riski almak istemiyorum.

    I don't want to take this risk.

    Risk almak = to take a risk; riskli = risky.

    B1

  56. 856
    canavarnoun

    monster; beast

    Yatağın altında canavar yok, uyu artık.

    There's no monster under the bed; go to sleep now.

    Also said of a cruel person: O adam bir canavar!

    B1

  57. 857
    sınırnoun

    border; limit

    Sabrımın da bir sınırı var!

    My patience has its limits too!

    Sınır kapısı = border crossing; sınırlı = limited; sınırsız = unlimited.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 2: -DIr: assumption and authority

  58. 858
    abinoun

    older brother; a friendly way to address a man a little older than you

    Abi, bu otobüs Kadıköy'e gidiyor mu?

    Excuse me, does this bus go to Kadıköy?

    The spoken form of ağabey. To a brother, or as friendly address to a man a bit older: Ali abi (lowercase after a name). The female counterpart is abla.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 9: Everyday colloquial Turkish

  59. 859
    duanoun

    prayer

    Büyükannem her akşam dua eder.

    My grandmother prays every evening.

    Dua etmek = to pray; senin için dua edeceğim = I'll pray for you. Also said of good wishes for someone.

    B1

  60. 860
    çiçeknoun

    flower

    Annene çiçek aldın mı?

    Did you buy flowers for your mom?

    accusative çiçeği

    The k becomes ğ before a vowel: çiçeği. Çiçek açmak = to bloom; çiçekçi = florist.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 12: Requests and company

  61. 861
    çılgınadjective

    crazy, mad; wild

    Bu çılgın bir fikir, ama hoşuma gitti.

    That's a crazy idea, but I like it.

    Often admiring: çılgın bir parti (a wild party). Çılgınlık = madness. The everyday word for mad is deli.

    B1

  62. 862
    korkutmakverb

    to frighten, to scare

    Beni çok korkuttun!

    You really scared me!

    aorist korkutur · present korkutuyor · past korkuttu · future korkutacak

    Causative of korkmak (to be afraid). The person scared takes the accusative: çocukları korkutma.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 11: Causative and reciprocal

  63. 863
    salakadjective

    stupid, idiotic; idiot (noun)

    Kendimi salak gibi hissettim.

    I felt like an idiot.

    Colloquial, and rude when said to someone: Salak! Close to aptal. The k becomes ğ before a vowel: Ne kadar salağım! (How stupid of me!).

    B1

  64. 864
    topraknoun

    soil, earth; land, territory; ground

    Bu toprak domates için çok iyi.

    This soil is very good for tomatoes.

    accusative toprağı

    The k becomes ğ before a vowel: toprağı. The plural topraklar often means lands, territory.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 1: Stacked modality

  65. 865
    taşınmakverb

    to move (house); to be carried

    Geçen ay yeni bir eve taşındık.

    We moved to a new house last month.

    aorist taşınır · present taşınıyor · past taşındı · future taşınacak

    Passive or reflexive of taşımak (to carry). Where you move to takes the dative: İzmir'e taşınmak.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 2: Used to, was going to, should have

  66. 866
    ormannoun

    forest, woods

    Hafta sonu ormanda yürüyüş yaptık.

    We went hiking in the forest on the weekend.

    Orman yangını = forest fire; ormanlık = wooded.

    A2

  67. 867
    uzaklaşmakverb

    to move away, to go away; to drift apart

    Lütfen kapıdan uzaklaşın.

    Please move away from the door.

    aorist uzaklaşır · present uzaklaşıyor · past uzaklaştı · future uzaklaşacak

    From uzak (far) + -lAş. What you move away from takes the ablative. Also of people: Zamanla uzaklaştık (We drifted apart over time).

    B1

  68. 868
    tarznoun

    style; manner, way; kind, type

    Bu benim tarzım değil.

    This isn't my style.

    Giyim tarzı = style of dress; bu tarz şeyler = things like this.

    B1

  69. 869
    sevginoun

    love, affection

    Çocuklara sevgi ve sabır lazım.

    Children need love and patience.

    From sevmek. Calmer and broader than aşk (romantic love): love for family, friends, animals. Sevgiler closes a friendly message (Love, …).

    B1

  70. 870
    acımakverb

    to hurt, to be sore; to feel sorry for, to pity (dative)

    Ayağım çok acıyor.

    My foot really hurts.

    aorist acır · present acıyor · past acıdı · future acıyacak

    What hurts is the subject: Dizim acıyor (My knee hurts); for aches, ağrımak. With the dative, to pity: Ona acıyorum. Not acıkmak (to get hungry).

    A2

  71. 871
    sıkadverb

    often, frequently

    Buraya sık gelir misin?

    Do you come here often?

    Usually doubled: sık sık = often. As an adjective, dense or close together: sık bir orman. Not sıkı (tight, strict).

    A2

  72. 872
    yanılmakverb

    to be wrong, to be mistaken

    Galiba yanıldım, özür dilerim.

    I think I was wrong; I'm sorry.

    aorist yanılır · present yanılıyor · past yanıldı · future yanılacak

    Of a person's judgment: Yanılıyorsun (You're wrong). Yanılmıyorsam = If I'm not mistaken. A wrong answer is yanlış.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 2: -DIr: assumption and authority

  73. 873
    burunnoun

    nose; cape, headland

    Eczaneden burun spreyi aldım.

    I bought some nasal spray at the pharmacy.

    accusative burnu

    The u drops before a vowel: burnu, burnum. Burnum akıyor = My nose is running; burun kıvırmak = to turn up your nose.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 9: My family

  74. 874
    bağırmakverb

    to shout, to yell; to scream

    Bana bağırma, lütfen!

    Please don't shout at me!

    aorist bağırır · present bağırıyor · past bağırdı · future bağıracak

    Who you shout at takes the dative: çocuklara bağırmak. Bağırış = a shout, shouting.

    B1First taught in B1 · Unit 12: Reported speech

  75. 875
    kulüpnoun

    club

    Oğlum bir futbol kulübünde oynuyor.

    My son plays for a soccer club.

    accusative kulübü

    The p becomes b before a vowel: kulübü. Futbol kulübü = soccer club; gece kulübü = nightclub.

    B1

  76. 876
    defolmakverb

    to get lost, to clear off (rude); to go away (rude)

    Defol, seni bir daha görmek istemiyorum!

    Get lost, I don't want to see you again!

    aorist defolur · present defoluyor · past defoldu · future defolacak

    Rude, mostly in the imperative: Defol!, Defolun!, Defol git! Frequent in dubbed films; best avoided in real life.

    B1

  77. 877
    altınnoun

    gold; gold coin

    Bu yüzük gerçek altın mı?

    Is this ring real gold?

    Also an adjective: altın yüzük (gold ring). Small gold coins (çeyrek altın) are a traditional wedding present.

    A2First taught in A2 · Unit 12: Word building

  78. 878
    itirafnoun

    confession, admission

    Bir itirafım var: pastayı ben yedim.

    I have a confession: I ate the cake.

    İtiraf etmek = to confess, to admit: Suçunu itiraf etti. İtiraf etmeliyim ki… = I must admit that…

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 3: Although, despite, without

    ameliyatnoun

    operation, surgery

    Babam yarın ameliyat olacak.

    Ameliyat olmak = to have an operation; ameliyat etmek = to operate on someone.

  80. 880
    şekernoun

    sugar; candy, sweets

    Çayına şeker ister misin?

    Do you want sugar in your tea?

    Şekerli = with sugar; şekersiz = without. Colloquially also diabetes: Babamda şeker var. Şeker Bayramı = the holiday at the end of Ramadan.

    church

    There's an old church in the middle of the village.

    A mosque is a cami (camii with the possessive); a synagogue is a sinagog (also havra).

    düşüncenoun

    thought, idea; opinion

    Bu konuda düşüncen ne?

    What's your opinion on this?

    From düşünmek. Not düşününce (when you think). Düşünceli = thoughtful; also worried.

    C1First taught in C1 · Unit 3: Complex nominalizations

    televizyonnoun

    television, TV

    Akşamları televizyon izlemem.

    I don't watch TV in the evenings.

    Televizyon izlemek (or seyretmek) = to watch TV; televizyonda = on TV.

    öpmekverb

    to kiss

    Annem beni yanağımdan öptü.

    My mom kissed me on the cheek.

    aorist öper · present öpüyor · past öptü · future öpecek

    Where takes the ablative: yanağından öpmek (to kiss on the cheek). Öpüşmek = to kiss each other. Öptüm closes a message to family or friends (Kisses).

    A2

    Kuzeyde = in the north; Kuzey Amerika = North America. The others: güney, doğu, batı.

    ikna etmekverb

    to convince, to persuade

    Onu gelmeye ikna ettim.

    I convinced her to come.

    aorist ikna eder · present ikna ediyor · past ikna etti · future ikna edecek

    What you persuade someone to do takes the dative: gelmeye ikna etmek. İkna olmak = to be convinced.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 3: Although, despite, without

    Çorabımda büyük bir delik var.

    There's a big hole in my sock.

    accusative deliği

    From delmek (to pierce). The k becomes ğ before a vowel: deliği. Delikli = with holes. Not deli (crazy).

    düzeltmekverb

    to correct, to fix; to straighten, to tidy

    From düz (straight, flat). Düzelmek = to get better, by itself: Hava düzeldi (The weather has cleared up).

    married

    Are you married or single?

    Ev (home) + -lI. Evlenmek = to get married (to: ile); evlilik = marriage.

    A1First taught in A1 · Unit 3: Saying who you are

  90. 890
    yabancıadjective

    foreign; strange, unfamiliar; foreigner; stranger (noun)

    As a noun, a foreigner or a stranger: Yabancılarla konuşma (Don't talk to strangers). Yabancı dil = foreign language.

    B2First taught in B2 · Unit 2: As if

    binmekverb

    aorist biner · present biniyor · past bindi · future binecek

    paylaşmakverb

    aorist paylaşır · present paylaşıyor · past paylaştı · future paylaşacak

    With whom: ile. From pay (share, portion). Also on social media: fotoğraf paylaşmak.

    kokmakverb

    The thing gives off the smell: Bu süt kokuyor (This milk smells bad). To smell something yourself is koklamak; a smell is koku.

    adımnoun

    I work freelance; I don't have an office.

    Free as in not held or not restricted: Polis onu serbest bıraktı (The police released him). Free of charge is ücretsiz or bedava; free time is boş.

About this list

The words are ranked by how often they come up in film and TV dialogue, so the list leans towards spoken Turkish. Words are listed in their dictionary form (verbs in the infinitive, gelmek), names and fragments are left out, and ranks are estimates rather than exact counts.

The order of the list is adapted from the 2018 Turkish list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave, made from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus via OPUS, and is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. The meanings, example sentences and notes are original to Daily Turkish.
